Email is the best way to reach me directly: [r.lovelace@leeds.ac.uk](mailto:r.lovelace@leeds.ac.uk).
A short message saying who you are and what you would like to do together helps me reply quickly.

## Study and research {#study-and-research}

I am interested in hearing from prospective PhD and Masters students working on transport data science, active travel, open data and open-source tools for planning.

- See the Institute for Transport Studies [research degrees page](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/transport-research-degrees) for funding and how to apply.
- The [Transport Data Science](https://github.com/ITSLeeds/tds) module gives a flavour of the methods I teach.
- When you email, include a few sentences on your research idea, how it links to my [publications](/publications/) or [projects](/projects/), and your CV.

## Collaboration {#collaboration}

I work with public bodies, charities, companies and other researchers on data, models and tools for sustainable transport, from national planning tools to city-level studies.
See [current projects](/projects/) for examples, then email me with an outline of your question, data or idea.

## Software and methods questions {#software}

I get many questions about software, and asking in public is usually best:

- Open an issue or discussion on the relevant [GitHub](https://github.com/robinlovelace) repository.
  You are likely to get a quicker answer, and other people can benefit from it.
- I prioritise well-asked questions with a reproducible example.
- For geographic data science with R or Python, join the geocompx Discord:
  [![discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/878051191374876683?label=discord&logo=Discord&color=blue)](https://discord.gg/PMztXYgNxp)

## Talks and media {#talks-and-media}

I speak about open tools, transport data and reproducible research at conferences, workshops and training events.
See [past and upcoming events](/events/), then email me with the date, audience and format.
